response:
This sounds really painful—wanting to be part of your grandchild's life and feeling shut out is a hard place to be, especially when you thought things had improved between you and your son.

It's worth remembering that four weeks postpartum is often an exhausting, overwhelming time for new parents, and their quietness may have less to do with you than it seems. Rather than waiting and stewing, you might reach out warmly and without pressure—a simple message saying you'd love to see them and the baby whenever they're up for it, no expectations. That keeps the door open while respecting that they're finding their footing.

If old tensions are part of this, it may help to lead with connection rather than any hint of the past disagreements. You can't control their response, but you can offer warmth and let them know you're there. That's a genuine gift, even if it takes time for them to reach back.
